stem:
The diagram shows quadrilateral $PQRS$ with both pairs of opposite sides parallel. Bina asks how rectangles and squares relate to parallelograms.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: $PQRS$ is a parallelogram; rectangles and squares are special parallelograms because their opposite sides are parallel.
$PQRS$ is a parallelogram only if all four angles are $90^{\circ}$.
The same rule classifies any open path of four segments as a parallelogram.

teacher.key_rationale: Both pairs of opposite sides parallel make a parallelogram; rectangles and squares sit inside that set. Requiring four right angles adds an unneeded condition. Saying every parallelogram is a square reverses the inclusion. Open paths are outside the closed-quadrilateral scope.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source as parallelogram PQRS with opposite sides parallel.
